subject: Access Fence proposal: BYOK telemetry minimization & operator access commitments
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helixhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Access fence — BYOK telemetry and limited operator visibility

Neha — thanks for the call today. As discussed, Helix needs a short paper we can attach to our DPA addendum that explains operator telemetry minimization for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) when the customer manages keys. Our key asks are: 

- Redwood will not persist model-level or request-level plaintext customer data in centrally accessible logs. Any runtime telemetry captured for the platform must be irreversibly pseudonymized or hashed, with retention <= 30 days by default.
- Operator access to the keystore and any key material is strictly limited to emergency break-glass with recorded, time-limited sessions and prior notification to Helix where feasible.
- Audit logs demonstrating these controls (sample schema) so Helix can satisfy our internal auditors.

Can you provide a short Access Fence annex we can circulate? Attaching our standard DPA excerpt for context.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Security Program Manager, Helix Health
Attachments: helix_dpa_excerpt.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access fence — BYOK telemetry and limited operator visibility

Emma — really appreciate the clear list. I’ve drafted an "Access Fence Annex" that aligns with Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) BYOK deployments and includes:

1) Telemetry minimization commitments (data categories, granularity, pseudonymization approach, retention windows).
2) Keystore/escrow operator access policy (break-glass workflow, approvals, just-in-time session, MFA + ephemeral creds).
3) Audit log schema and a sample CSV export (no plaintext customer prompts; only hashed request IDs, timestamps, operator session IDs).
4) Cross-border transfer statement limited to control-plane metadata and only when necessary for support (with customer opt-in).

I attached the draft annex and a small sample of the audit export. Please review and let us know if this covers Helix's ask or if you want tighter retention or different pseudonymization.

I’ve looped Jonas for technical ops specifics and Laura for legal consumability. Ben — can you confirm we can produce the audit CSV on a 30-day retention default and provide a proof sample?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Access_Fence_Annex_v1.pdf; audit_log_sample.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access fence — BYOK telemetry and limited operator visibility

Neha / Laura — quick tech notes for the annex: 

- Telemetry: We currently capture runtime metrics (token throughput, memory pressure), anonymized request latencies, and error counts. We do not persist request payloads for Private BYOK deployments unless a customer explicitly enables support logging.
- Pseudonymization approach: our deterministic hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant salt stored in customer environment for on-prem) converts request IDs; sample CSV includes hashed_request_id.
- Keystore access: for customer-managed keys (BYOK) we do not store private keys in Redwood-managed HSMs. Operator access is limited to remote orchestration metadata; any operator actions that require key use are executed by customer-controlled gateways or via signed token exchange — we can describe the JIT session flow.
- Retention: default 30d for minimal telemetry; support escalation can extend to 90d with customer authorization. We can make 30d mandatory in the DPA annex if Helix requires it.

I attached an internal diagram link in the doc; happy to add a step-by-step runbook for break-glass if legal wants the exact approval flow.

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helixhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Igor Petrov <igor.petrov@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access fence — BYOK telemetry and limited operator visibility

Thanks — the draft is very helpful. A few clarifying asks from our auditors and CISO: 

- Can Redwood commit to a contractual clause that operator sessions for BYOK keystore operations will require: (a) dual human approval from two distinct Redwood operators, or (b) customer-initiated approval via their control plane, where feasible?
- For pseudonymization: we want explicit assurance that pseudonymized request IDs cannot be reversed by Redwood. Can you include the HMAC salt handling (stored on customer side/on-prem) and a sentence that says Redwood does not retain the salt?
- Cross-border: please add a declarative statement that no plaintext request data will leave the customer VPC/on-prem unless explicitly package-signed and approved for transfer by Helix.

Attached: our redline to the annex (short comments inline).

Emma

Attachment: redline_Access_Fence_Annex.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helixhealth.com>, Igor Petrov <igor.petrov@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access fence — BYOK telemetry and limited operator visibility

Emma / Igor — thank you for the precise redlines; we can accept the majority of these requests and propose the following final commitments for the Access Fence Annex: 

1) Dual-approval or customer-initiated approval: for operator activities that would require use of customer keys or decryption, Redwood will (at customer election) either: 
   - require dual Redwood operator approval (two distinct operators), recorded and auditable; or
   - require an API call from the customer control plane to unlock the operation (customer-initiated JIT). We will document both flows and allow Helix to select the default in the addendum.

2) Salt handling and pseudonymization: the HMAC salt used to pseudonymize request IDs for Private BYOK will be generated and stored by the customer. Redwood will not persist or have access to that salt. We will include a non-reversible pseudonymization statement in the annex.

3) Data egress: the annex will state: "Redwood will not transfer plaintext customer request or model data out of the customer VPC/on-prem environment except with express, auditable customer authorization. Platform control-plane metadata required for multi-region routing or health diagnostics may be transmitted after pseudonymization and under the retention terms below."

4) Retention windows: default telemetry retention of 30 days. Extended retention up to 90 days only with documented customer approval (signed link or DocuSign).

5) Evidence package: Redwood will provide an audit sample (CSV) and a runbook for break-glass sessions. We will produce the audit sample within 5 business days upon Helix's request during procurement review.

Next steps: Laura and I will fold these commitments into Access_Fence_Annex_v2 and circulate with a DocuSign link for Helix's selection of the operator-approval model (dual-operator vs customer-initiated). Ben will coordinate the sample audit export.

If that sounds correct we can move to legal redline acceptance and procurement.

Thanks,
Neha
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
